headline: Jensen Huang resigned and NVDA closed down 4.3% after falling 14% at the open; the bigger problem is rates: the 30 year sale tailed and the 10 year closed at 5.10%, so stay patient into Nvidia's Nov 17 report.
summary: Data note: the dashboard still shows Nov 11 closes (meta.json says the Nov 12 session is missing) and Massive failed to connect today, so every Nov 12 level here is from Yahoo Finance daily bars and is labeled. Nvidia said before Thursday's open that its CEO resigned from the company and the board; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey Jones the first board chair (CNBC). NVDA hit 148.80 at the open, then closed 166.19, down 4.34%, on 742.8 million shares, about 5.6 times normal; AMD rose 5.86% and AVGO 5.54% (Yahoo). The market slipped: SPY fell 0.35% and QQQ 0.32% to 688.17, still 0.65% over its 683.69 line but on only 36.7 million shares (Yahoo). Rates did more damage: the $25 billion 30 year sale tailed at 5.441%, the 10 year closed near 5.10% and the 2 year at 4.867% (investingLive; Reuters). This morning October producer prices came in cooler than expected (0.3% vs 0.4%), Cisco, Applied Materials and Cerebras beat after the close, and the put screen could not run because Massive is down.

regime.why: The Nvidia question has an answer, and the market absorbed it: the S&P 500 fell only 0.35%. But long rates rose on a second weak auction, and QQQ held its line on light volume. Stay mixed until QQQ closes over 683.69 on 55 million or more shares and the 10 year stops climbing.

signals.title: Jensen Huang resigns; Kress is interim CEO; NVDA closes down 4.3% after a 14% drop at the open
signals.since_yesterday: The board decision came: at about 8:48am ET Thursday Nvidia said its CEO resigned from the company and the board, effective at once (StockTitan; CNBC).
signals.what_happened: CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches, and former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones becomes Nvidia's first board chair (CNBC). NVDA opened at 151.01, hit 148.80, and closed 166.19, down 4.34%, on 742.8 million shares, about 5.6 times its recent average (Yahoo). It closed above the $164 floor it broke before the open. Reuters reported a third relationship, with an unnamed employee, on Thursday (via CNBC). Nvidia still reports Nov 17 (MarketScreener; TradingKey). The Senate Banking chair asked the former CEO and the Commerce Secretary to testify in December (Investing.com via Yahoo). Analysts cut targets: Truist to $174 from $346 with a Hold, Morgan Stanley to $267 from $300, Bernstein to $200 from $400 (MarketScreener; CNBC). NVDA traded about 1.7% higher at 8:13am ET Friday (CNBC).
signals.so_what: The worst case of a slow, messy fight is off the table, which is why the stock recovered most of its open. Second order: the outlook on Nov 17 now comes from a CFO, not the founder, and customers testing other chips have a reason to spread orders. AMD and AVGO rose about 5.5% to 5.9% on that bet. Third order: Nvidia is about 10% of the Nasdaq 100 (Fortune), so its report moves QQQ and every AI supplier. Reuters says it trades near 12 times expected earnings, its lowest since 2012. What would make this wrong: a strong Nov 17 guide and a fast permanent pick.
signals.for_you: No NVDA trade or put before Nov 17; it stays 'Wait'. AMD closed 585.30 (Yahoo), now 3.2% over its 525.17 to 566.94 zone, so it is not a buy. No new AI swings until Nov 19.

signals.title: The 30 year sale tailed and the 10 year closed at 5.10%; producer prices came in a bit cooler
signals.since_yesterday: Thursday's 30 year auction stopped at 5.441%, a 0.4 basis point tail, with a 2.36 bid to cover, the second soft sale this week. The 10 year rose about 11.6 basis points to 5.10%.
signals.what_happened: Bid to cover fell to 2.36 from 2.54 in October; foreign style (indirect) bidders took 68.1% versus 72.3%, and dealers were left with 11.4% (investingLive). The 10 year closed at 5.105% and the 2 year at 4.867%, both multi week highs (Reuters). Jobless claims rose 9,000 to 200,000 (StockTitan). New York Fed President Williams said more hikes are likely without naming size or timing (investingLive). Futures price about 29 basis points of hikes by December (Reuters). This morning October producer prices rose 0.3%, under the 0.4% forecast, and 6.5% from a year ago, the most since November 2022; prices less food, energy and trade rose 0.5% (Securities.io; TokenPost).
signals.so_what: Two weak sales in a week say buyers want more yield to hold long US debt. That raises the cost of every AI build funded with debt and pressures utilities and small caps: IWM fell 1.64% Thursday (StockTitan). The cooler producer number helps a little but does not change a December hike. What would make this wrong: yields falling back under 5% on the PPI miss.
signals.for_you: Puts: the bar is now about 5.1% a year. Long term: AEP closed 128.91, still 1.4% over its zone top, and rate sensitive; wait for a dip into its 122.73 to 127.12 zone. Swing: small caps lag, so skip small cap breakouts.

signals.title: Cisco, Applied Materials and Cerebras all beat and raised; the stocks barely moved except Cerebras
signals.since_yesterday: Results are out. Cisco and Applied Materials beat and guided above estimates; Cerebras rose about 18% after hours.
signals.what_happened: Cisco: revenue $18.5 billion, up 24%, versus $18.1 billion expected; adjusted EPS $1.40 versus $1.33; next quarter guide $18.0 to $18.2 billion versus $17.88 billion; it now expects $9 billion of AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers this fiscal year, more than double last year (CNBC). Orders grew 21%, down from 35% the prior quarter (Investing.com via Yahoo). CSCO was down about 1.7% before the open (Benzinga). Applied Materials: record revenue of $10.41 billion, up 53%; adjusted EPS $4.16; it guided about $11.1 billion next quarter versus $10.89 billion expected (company; Investing.com via Yahoo). AMAT closed 380.95, down 3.58%, before the report, and was about flat after hours (Yahoo; StockTitan). Cerebras: revenue $210.8 million, up 55%, and a raised full year outlook; it rose about 18% after hours and about 16% before the open from a 97.75 close (StockTitan; TradingKey; Yahoo).
signals.so_what: AI demand is still real at the tool and network level the day the AI leader lost its CEO. Second order: Cisco's slowing order growth is a sign the easy part of the network upgrade is done. Applied's guide says chip makers keep building into 2027. Third order: if spending holds, the money flows to tools and networking even if Nvidia's share slips. What would make this wrong: Nvidia guiding down on Nov 17.
signals.for_you: No action. None of the three is a setup or a buy zone name; CSCO is 'Wait' (102.01 on Nov 12, Yahoo). Do not chase CBRS after an 18% gap. ANET, on the buy list, closed 206.63, up 5.06% on about 1.5 times normal volume (Yahoo), now 4.3% over its 198.17 zone top, so it is no longer a buy at this price.

signals.title: MP Materials: the COO, CFO and a director bought $3.35 million after a 44% slide
signals.what_happened: Three MP Materials insiders bought on Nov 10, filed Nov 12: director Randall Weisenburger about $1.98 million at $36.00 (his stake up 36%), COO Michael Rosenthal about $1.18 million at $36.72, and CFO Ryan Corbett about $199,000 at $36.25 (dashboard from SEC Form 4s; GuruFocus). The stock was down 44% over six months and 52% under its $76.80 high (GuruFocus). MP closed 37.45, up 1.96%, on 8.6 million shares, about 1.6 times normal, on Nov 12 (Yahoo).
signals.so_what: A cluster that includes the COO and CFO is the strongest insider signal there is. MP is the main US rare earth miner and magnet maker, a chokepoint in the critical materials map, and China's metal export pause ends Nov 27. Second order: the insiders are betting the price drop overshot while US magnet output ramps. What would make this wrong: China extending its waivers and flooding the market, which would keep rare earth prices low.
signals.for_you: Watch only. MP is not a setup and not on the buy list, and it is down hard, so this is not a buy signal by itself. If it builds a base and the chart turns, it could become a swing candidate. Filing is 1 day old.

signals.title: Oil: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi oil sites and Iran says four tankers burned; Brent settles $95.82
signals.since_yesterday: Brent settled up $3.06, or 3.3%, at $95.82 Thursday after Houthi claims of drone strikes on Saudi oil sites and reports of tankers hit near Hormuz (Reuters via Euronext).
signals.what_happened: The Houthis claimed drone strikes on an Aramco site in Riyadh, the Yanbu refinery and an East West pipeline pumping station; the Saudi led coalition said it shot down two drones, and no damage was confirmed (House of Saud; The New Arab). Iran's military said four tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz (The New Arab). Friday morning Brent held just under $96 after the IEA said supply now exceeds demand for the first time since the war began (Invezz). XLE rose 1.51% to 64.33 on Nov 12 (Yahoo).
signals.so_what: Oil is pulled two ways: attacks add a risk premium, while the IEA sees a surplus. That keeps prices jumpy, not trending. Higher oil feeds the producer price numbers the Fed watches.
signals.for_you: No energy setups or energy puts. No action.

signals.title: Alibaba fell 7% on fears it loses access to Nvidia chips rented abroad
signals.what_happened: BABA fell about 7% in US trading and 6.8% in Hong Kong on Nov 12 (Reuters via MarketScreener; Quartz). Bloomberg reported Alibaba rents Nvidia chips through Singapore based Megaspeed, and the Commerce Department is said to be finishing rules to stop Chinese AI developers from reaching advanced chips in data centers abroad (Bloomberg; Quartz).
signals.so_what: The Nvidia probe started with a China link, so the next policy step is likely tighter rules on who can rent US chips. Second order: that would cut a source of Nvidia demand in Southeast Asia and push Chinese firms to Huawei. What would make this wrong: no rule issued before the Trump and Xi meeting at APEC.
signals.for_you: No action. No Chinese ADR is on the buy list. It is one more reason to avoid NVDA before Nov 17.

cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening. The Fed's range is 3.75% to 4% and futures price about 29 basis points more by December (Reuters). Williams said more hikes are likely (investingLive). The 2 year rose to 4.867%.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Two soft Treasury sales in a week, with the 30 year at 5.441% and dealers taking more (investingLive). The government pays over 5% to borrow for 10 and 30 years.
cycle.big_cycle: Technology and internal order: the largest AI chip company lost its founder CEO in a week, and the Senate wants testimony on its China ties. External order: Houthi and Iranian attacks keep Gulf oil at risk, and the US moves to close chip access for Chinese firms abroad.
tailwinds: AI suppliers beat and raised: Cisco expects $9 billion of AI revenue this year.
The market absorbed the CEO exit: the S&P 500 fell only 0.35%.

headwinds: Long Treasury sales are weak and the 10 year is at 5.10%.

history.what: Apple stock rose about $1 a share when his resignation became known, and analysts said they saw no problems (San Francisco Chronicle archive, Sep 19, 1985). Apple then lagged for years until he returned in 1997.
history.lesson: The first day reaction to a founder leaving says little. Execution over the next few quarters decides it. Nvidia's Nov 17 guide is the first test.

source.title: Jobs' departure won't affect Apple; analysts foresee no problems (San Francisco Chronicle archive, Sep 19, 1985)

history.when: February 1994 to February 1995: the Fed's surprise tightening
history.what: The Fed doubled its target from 3% to 6% in a year and US bond losses reached about $600 billion by late 1994 (Fortune).
history.lesson: Weak auctions and rising long yields came before the stock pain. This week brought two weak sales.

cycle.differences: Apple in 1985 had a weak product line; Nvidia today has record sales and a CFO who knows the numbers. The bigger risk this time is the price of money, not the company's demand.
cycle.for_you: Swing: stand aside until QQQ confirms on volume and Nvidia reports; TMO is the only setup and it is fading. Puts: the screen could not run today. Long term: in zone names (PODD, LDOS, TMUS, RELY) only in small first tranches, and not before Nov 17.

principle.text: Don't confuse what you wish were true with what is really true (paraphrase of Principles).
